extracted.intended_audience: Users of MetaPost (graphics programmers / TeX users) writing MetaPost figure source
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and syntax rules for writing MetaPost programs to produce graphics and integrate text (including TeX labels). Covers data types, operators, tokenization, variable declarations, fonts, label processing, and fill/color semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: String constant form and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: String constants are given in double quotes "like this" and cannot contain double quotes or newlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: String constants cannot start on one line and end on a later line; they cannot contain anything other than printable ASCII characters. There is a way to construct strings containing any sequence of eight-bit characters (described elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting strings to tokens (scantokens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion from strings to other types, notably numeric, can be accomplished by the scantokens primitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use n := scantokens(str); since scantokens parses a string into a token sequence as if MetaPost had read it as input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean and comparison operators
rubrics_metrics.description: The boolean type has the constants true and false and the operators and, or, not. The relations = and <> test objects of any type for equality and inequality. Comparison relations <, <=, >, >= are defined lexicographically for strings and in the obvious way for numerics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering relations are also defined for booleans, pairs, colors, and transforms, but comparison rules for those are not discussed in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture data type and currentpicture
rubrics_metrics.description: The picture data type stores anything that can be drawn in MetaPost. The draw statement actually stores its results in a special picture variable called currentpicture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pictures can be added to other pictures and operated on by transforms; use picture variables to manipulate drawn content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pens and pickup pen
rubrics_metrics.description: A data type called pen determines line thickness and can achieve calligraphic effects. The statement pickup <pen expression> causes the given pen to be used in subsequent draw or drawdot statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally the pen expression is of the form pencircle scaled <numeric primary> to produce circular pens of constant thickness. The pen expression can be adjusted to give elliptical or polygonal pens as desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression precedence (primary/secondary/tertiary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressions use four levels of precedence: primaries, secondaries, tertiaries, and expressions, allowing result type to depend on operator and operand types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax rules (Figure 15) define constructions like ⟨primary⟩ → ⟨variable⟩ | (⟨expression⟩) | ⟨nullary op⟩ | ⟨of operator⟩⟨expression⟩of⟨primary⟩ | ⟨unary op⟩⟨primary⟩. If operand types do not match an operator, an error message results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary binops: multiplication, division, exponentiation, dotprod
rubrics_metrics.description: * and / are primary binops that accept numeric operands or numeric with pair/color; ** is a primary binop requiring two numeric operands. dotprod is a primary binop computing vector dot product of two pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because ** shares precedence with * and /, expressions like 3*a**2 parse as (3a)2; be careful with unary negation and exponentiation (-a**2 means (-a)2). dotprod behaves like x1*x2 + y1*y2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additive and boolean binops precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Additive operators + and - are secondary binops operating on numerics, pairs, or colors and produce results of same type. The and operator is a primary binop and the or operator is a secondary binop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other operators in the secondary/tertiary categories (e.g., Pythagorean ++ and +-+) operate on compatible types; check operator category when combining operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: String operations: concatenation, length, substring indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Concatenation uses & (a ⟨tertiary binop⟩). length returns number of characters for a ⟨string primary⟩. substring uses 'substring <pair expression> of <string primary>' with string indexed so integer positions fall between characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing convention: first character occupies x in (0,1), so substring (2,4) of "abcde" is "cd"; this convention avoids off-by-one errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullary operator example (nullpicture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some operators take no arguments; e.g., nullpicture returns a completely blank picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullary ops can be used where a picture value is required but emptiness is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path-specific syntax (path knot rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Path syntax provides alternative rules; e.g., ⟨path knot⟩ → ⟨pair tertiary⟩ | ⟨path tertiary⟩ so path expressions sometimes don't need parentheses around constructs like z1+(1,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the path syntax (Figure 13) for allowable path primary/secondary constructions when writing path expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation expressions and numeric atom rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Mediation expressions are parsed at the primary level with general rule ⟨primary⟩ → ⟨numeric atom⟩[⟨expression⟩,⟨expression⟩] where each expression can be numeric, pair, or color. A ⟨numeric atom⟩ is an extra simple numeric primary; initial parameter needs parentheses when not a variable, a positive number, or a positive fraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: -1[a,b] is -(1[a,b]) = -b, while (-1)[a,b] is a - (b - a) = 2a - b. Numeric primary/atom grammar (Figure 16) clarifies which forms are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division binding with numeric operands
rubrics_metrics.description: The / operator binds most tightly when its operands are numbers: 2/3 is a ⟨numeric atom⟩ while (1+1)/3 is a ⟨numeric secondary⟩.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impacts parsing of unary operators: sqrt 2/3 means sqrt(2)/3 while sqrt(1+1)/3 means sqrt(1+1)/3; add parentheses where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary operators can accept non-numeric types
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all unary operators take numeric arguments and return numeric results: e.g., abs applied to a pair returns Euclidean length; unitvector rescales pair to length 1; decimal returns string representation; angle returns arctangent; cycle applied to a path returns boolean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate unary ops for different operand types; type-testing unary ops (see another criterion) help ensure correct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type-testing and known/unknown operators
rubrics_metrics.description: A type name such as pair can operate as a unary operator on any primary and return boolean indicating whether the argument is a pair. Similarly numeric, boolean, cmykcolor, color, string, transform, path, pen, picture, and rgbcolor are available. known and unknown test if a primary has a completely known value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tests to guard operations or to branch based on runtime knowledge of values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers may act like operators in some contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: A number or fraction that is not followed by +, -, or another number/fraction can serve as a ⟨primary binop⟩, allowing 3x and 3cm as alternatives to 3*x and 3*cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with parentheses: 2/3x is two thirds of x, whereas parenthesization changes meaning; avoid ambiguous constructs to prevent parsing surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracting numeric subfields (xpart, ypart, redpart, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators exist for extracting numeric subfields from pairs, colors, cmykcolors, and transforms: xpart p, ypart p, redpart c, greenpart c, bluepart c, cyanpart/magentapart/yellowpart/blackpart for cmykcolor, greypart for greyscale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., (xpart p, ypart p) is equivalent to p even for unknown pairs; see sections 9.10 and 9.3 for more on color/transforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tokenization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost input is tokenized into numbers, string constants, and symbolic tokens. A number is a sequence of digits possibly containing a decimal point; the minus sign in front of negative numbers is a separate token; exponential notation like 6.02E23 is not understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic tokens are sequences of similar characters (similar defined by Table 1 rows). Period rules: .. and ... are symbolic tokens, a single period is ignored, a period next to digits is part of the number. Percent introduces comments to end of line. Use periods to separate tokens in multi-token variable names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable name syntax and suffix conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Variable names are symbolic tokens or sequences of tokens; compound names like z.a, x2r, z2r allowed where z⟨suffix⟩ abbreviates (x⟨suffix⟩, y⟨suffix⟩).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suffix is composed of tokens; use this to simulate records/arrays and to make figure-local naming: variables that start with x, y, z are local to beginfig...endfig blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable declarations and array syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations such as 'pair pp, a.b;' make pp and a.b unknown pairs. Variables like x2 and y2 default numeric; you cannot give explicit numeric subscripts in a variable declaration—use the generic subscript symbol [] to declare arrays (e.g., numeric q[]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can declare multidimensional arrays (path p[]q[], pq[][]). Declarations are not strictly local unless they use x/y naming conventions or other scoping mechanisms discussed later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal variables and newinternal
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal variables (e.g., tracingonline) are predefined and need not be declared. Use newinternal followed by optional type and tokens to declare variables that behave like newly-created internal variables, e.g., newinternal numeric n, m; newinternal string s, t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal numeric variables initially zero and internal string variables initially empty string (Plain macros may override). If type specifier is missing, newinternal defaults to numeric; newinternal numeric; and newinternal string; (with no names) are invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling primitives (label, dotlabel, thelabel) and suffixes
rubrics_metrics.description: label<suffix>(<string or picture expression>, <pair expression>) places a label; suffixes (empty, lft, rt, top, bot, ulft, urt, llft, lrt) control label position relative to coordinates; dotlabel places a dot and a label; thelabel returns a picture instead of drawing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use labeloffset to control amount of offset. dotlabels and labels macros provide shorthand forms (labels discouraged due to METAFONT compatibility). Use dotlabels.rt to generate many dotlabel.rt calls from suffix lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font selection and defaultscale/defaultfont
rubrics_metrics.description: String labels are typeset in the default font determined by internal variable defaultfont (initially e.g. "cmr10"); defaultscale determines type size (1 = normal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change defaultscale := 1.2 to enlarge labels. To set an absolute point size: defaultscale := 12pt/fontsize defaultfont; when changing defaultfont use a name TeX would understand because MetaPost reads tfm files to get metrics. MetaPost does not use ligatures/kerning info and does not interpret virtual fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using TeX for labels (btex ... etex and verbatimtex)
rubrics_metrics.description: btex <typesetting commands> etex blocks are processed by TeX and translated into picture expressions usable in label/dotlabel. verbatimtex ... etex adds material for TeX processing but does not produce a picture expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: btex blocks are collected into a temp file and processed by TeX; environment variable MPTEXPRE can prepend content; errors are saved in mpxerr.tex and messages in mpxerr.log. The DVI-to-MetaPost conversion understands virtual fonts; use MPXCOMMAND to delegate conversion if set. Use -troff to treat btex/verbatimtex as troff and set troffmode=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prologues variable and output/font embedding recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: prologues controls font embedding and output format: 0 (no embedded fonts), 1 (structured PostScript, deprecated), 2 (EPSF with re-encoding via fontmap), 3 (EPSF including PostScript font subset). SVG and other modes interpret prologues differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: for TeX+dvips set prologues to 0,2, or 3 (3 safest but larger files); for external PostScript applications set prologues to 3 to embed fonts; prologues has no effect for pdfTeX or PNG; SVG reliability for exporting text requires prologues=3 (glyphs converted to paths).

rubrics_metrics.name: Font map primitives (fontmapfile/fontmapline) and options
rubrics_metrics.description: fontmapfile and fontmapline provide font mapping for prologues=2 or 3, specifying map files or mapping entries; an optional leading flag +, =, - extends, replaces, or removes matching fonts from current list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no fontmapfile provided, MetaPost attempts mpost.map, then troff.map or pdftex.map depending on troffmode. prologues=1 uses psfonts.map for backward compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: infont operator for raw font rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: infont is a primary binop taking a ⟨string secondary⟩ (text) and a ⟨string primary⟩ (font name), returning a picture secondary. Example: char(n+64) infont "ptmr8r" is a picture containing that character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: label("text", z0) is equivalent to label("text" infont defaultfont scaled defaultscale, z0). Bare MetaPost does not do input reencoding when using infont, so strings must be in the font encoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring text and bounding-box operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Unary operators llcorner, lrcorner, urcorner, ulcorner, and center take a ⟨picture primary⟩ and return corners of its bounding box. bbox p macro returns rectangular path representing bounding box (with bboxmargin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TEX features that lie about box dimensions are implemented with setbounds ⟨picture variable⟩ to ⟨path expression⟩; set truecorners:=1 to get the true bounding box despite setbounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: fill statement and color models
rubrics_metrics.description: fill <path expression> fills a cyclic path; fill <path expression> withcolor <color expression> selects color. Color specifications map to color models (greyscale, rgb, cmyk or current default) via withrgbcolor, withcmykcolor, withgreyscale, withcolor <numeric>, withoutcolor, withcolor false/true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An image object cannot have more than one color model; the last withcolor/withrgbcolor/withcmykcolor/withgreyscale/withoutcolor sets the model. withoutcolor means MetaPost will not write a color selection statement to PostScript file. Use defaultcolormodel to set current default model. fill uses PostScript's non-zero winding number rule; ensure path is cyclic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill order semantics (fills overwrite previous content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each fill statement assigns the given color to all points in the region covered, wiping out whatever was there previously including lines and text as well as filled regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give fill commands in the right order to obtain desired layering (example: filling overlapping circles in sequence to get different shading in intersection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility macros for building and labeling (buildcycle, dotlabels, unfill bbox)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefined macros such as buildcycle (to build closed path from parts), dotlabels (shorthand for many dotlabel calls), and unfill bbox (to make space for picture labels) help manage common tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate using buildcycle to compute overlapping region paths, then using fill/unfill/draw and draw bbox currentpicture to compose final output.
